skill.name: ponyflash
skill.description: Generate images, videos, speech audio, and music using the PonyFlash Python SDK. Also handle local media editing with FFmpeg, including clip, concat, transcode, extract audio, frame capture, subtitle capability checks, and ASS subtitle prep. Use when the user asks to create, generate, produce, edit, trim, merge, concatenate, transcode, subtitle, or render AI-generated media content.
skill.summary: Create AI media with PonyFlash and process local video, audio, and subtitles with FFmpeg helpers.
skill.author: ponyflash

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code formatting, installation paths, FFmpeg command examples, and safely quoted helper scripts. I confirmed only the active font download URL assignments as low-risk network behavior and added a medium semantic finding for missing font integrity verification. No prompt injection text or malicious intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the expected font artifact with a SHA-256 checksum or signature check before using it in FFmpeg subtitle rendering.
Restrict PONYFLASH_NOTO_FONT_URL to trusted HTTPS hosts or require explicit user confirmation before using a custom font URL.
Recommend scoped or temporary PonyFlash keys and prefer existing environment variables over pasting long-lived keys into chat.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Runtime Font Download
semantic_findings.description: The font preparation script downloads NotoSansCJKsc-Regular.otf from public HTTPS endpoints, allows PONYFLASH_NOTO_FONT_URL to override the primary source, and media_ops uses the downloaded font for subtitle burn-in. There is no checksum or signature verification before the binary font is handed to FFmpeg/libass.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts clearly define network font URLs, an environment override, temporary font staging, and FFmpeg subtitle filter use. HTTPS is used, so the risk is supply-chain integrity rather than obvious malicious behavior.

content.user_title: Generate and Edit AI Media with PonyFlash
content.value_statement: AI media work often spans separate generation, editing, and subtitle tools. PonyFlash combines SDK guidance with FFmpeg workflows for images, videos, speech, music, and exports.
actual_capabilities: Guides PonyFlash SDK setup for image, video, speech, and music generation.
Checks PonyFlash API key validity and account credits before cloud generation tasks.
Maps local media requests to FFmpeg helper scripts for clipping, concatenation, transcoding, audio extraction, and frame capture.
Checks FFmpeg, ffprobe, subtitle filter, encoder, and profile support before editing workflows.
Builds adaptive ASS subtitle files from SRT or JSON subtitle events.
Burns subtitles into video while staging temporary files and preserving final outputs.
limitations: Cloud generation requires a valid PonyFlash API key and available credits.
Local editing requires installed FFmpeg and ffprobe binaries with needed codec or subtitle support.
Generated media quality and available model parameters depend on the PonyFlash service.
The bundled helpers do not replace full manual FFmpeg control for unusual production pipelines.

use_cases.title: Create campaign media assets
use_cases.description: Generate visuals, short videos, voice tracks, and background music for a campaign brief.

use_cases.title: Finish local video edits
use_cases.description: Trim clips, merge exports, transcode files, extract audio, or capture thumbnails with stable FFmpeg commands.

use_cases.title: Prepare subtitled deliverables
use_cases.description: Convert subtitle text into adaptive ASS layout and burn captions into final video files.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a simple image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PonyFlash to generate one 16:9 image of a modern product desk scene. Confirm API key readiness before generation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a short video concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan and generate a 4 second 16:9 video of a city sunrise. Suggest model settings and report credit usage after generation.

prompt_templates.title: Edit a local media file
prompt_templates.prompt: Check FFmpeg support, trim input.mp4 from 00:00:05 for 8 seconds, and save the final clip as clip.mp4.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a subtitled social clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a short voiceover, prepare portrait video subtitles from my SRT file, burn them into the video, and keep only the final export.

output_examples.input: Generate a product hero image for a launch page.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms API key readiness, selects an image model, submits the prompt, and returns the generated asset link with credit usage.

output_examples.input: Cut an 8 second clip and make it web ready.
output_examples.output: The skill checks FFmpeg support, stages temporary files, trims the source, transcodes the output, and reports the final file path.

output_examples.input: Burn these subtitles into my vertical video.
output_examples.output: The skill checks subtitle filter support, builds adaptive ASS captions, prepares temporary fonts, renders the final video, and removes temporary files.

best_practices: Confirm API key status, credit availability, and target model before any paid generation task.
Run FFmpeg capability checks before editing, subtitle, or export workflows.
Use temporary task directories for staged assets and remove them after final deliverables are verified.
anti_patterns: Do not paste long-lived production API keys when a scoped or temporary key is available.
Do not overwrite existing media outputs unless the user explicitly approves replacement.
Do not assume subtitle burn-in works without checking the FFmpeg subtitles filter first.

faq.question: Does PonyFlash require an API key?
faq.answer: Cloud generation requires a PonyFlash API key. Local FFmpeg editing tasks do not require that key.

faq.question: Can it edit existing local videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The included FFmpeg helpers support clipping, concatenation, transcoding, audio extraction, frame capture, and subtitle burn-in.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill environments.

faq.question: Can it create music and speech?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents PonyFlash SDK paths for speech synthesis and music generation when the account has credits.

faq.question: Does it keep temporary files?
faq.answer: The default workflows remove temporary subtitle files, font directories, concat lists, and partial outputs unless the user asks to keep them.

faq.question: Can users choose custom fonts for subtitles?
faq.answer: Yes. Users can pass explicit Latin and CJK font files, or use the default Noto Sans CJK SC workflow.
